article.title: Valmora dock workers walk out in 48-hour strike over crane automation
article.text: Around 4,000 dock workers at the port of Valmora stopped work at 6 a.m. on Monday, starting a 48-hour strike called by the Estravan Port Workers Union. The union opposes the port authority's plan to replace 30 manned cranes with remote-controlled ones by 2028, which it says would cost up to 900 jobs. Container ships were queuing outside the harbour by midday, and the port authority said around 60 vessels would be delayed. Union chair Mira Tobel said further strikes were possible if talks did not resume.

article.title: Estravan government calls for mediation as port strike delays 60 ships
article.text: Estrava's transport minister Lio Caradin on Monday urged the port authority of Valmora and the dock workers' union to accept a state mediator, hours after the 48-hour strike over crane automation began. Caradin said the delays to around 60 container ships were hurting exporters and offered to host talks in the capital on Wednesday. The union welcomed the offer but said the automation plan had to be on the table. The port authority said it would study the proposal.

article.title: Magnitude 6.4 earthquake strikes northern Kessaria, dozens injured
article.text: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck northern Kessaria early on Tuesday, the national seismological institute said. The quake hit at 4:12 a.m. local time at a depth of 10 kilometres, about 25 kilometres west of the town of Orsen. Regional authorities reported at least 37 people injured and several buildings collapsed in Orsen's old town. Rescue teams were searching the rubble, and schools in the province were closed for the day. Aftershocks of up to magnitude 4.8 were recorded.

article.title: Kessaria quake death toll rises to 12 as rescuers search Orsen ruins
article.text: The death toll from Tuesday's magnitude 6.4 earthquake in northern Kessaria has risen to 12, the interior ministry said on Wednesday. Rescuers pulled two survivors from a collapsed apartment block in Orsen overnight. The government declared a state of emergency for the province and released 50 million kessars in emergency aid. Around 1,200 residents spent the night in tents set up in the town's football stadium.

article.title: Lumenix 5.0 brings built-in vector search to the open-source database
article.text: The Lumenix project released version 5.0 of its open-source database on Thursday. The headline feature is built-in vector search, which lets developers store embeddings next to regular tables and query them with a new NEAREST operator. The release also drops support for the legacy storage engine and requires a migration for databases created before version 3. Project lead Sana Vey said the vector index was benchmarked at up to 40,000 queries per second on a single server.

article.title: Lumenix founder Sana Vey steps down as project lead
article.text: Sana Vey, who founded the Lumenix database project eleven years ago, announced on Monday that she is stepping down as project lead at the end of the year. In a blog post she said she wanted to spend more time on research and would remain on the project's steering committee. The steering committee will elect a successor in December. Vey's announcement came three weeks after the release of Lumenix 5.0.

article.title: Zentralbank von Estrava erhöht Leitzins auf 4,5 Prozent
article.text: Die Zentralbank von Estrava hat am Donnerstag ihren Leitzins um einen halben Prozentpunkt auf 4,5 Prozent angehoben. Es ist die dritte Erhöhung in diesem Jahr. Die Landeswährung legte nach der Ankündigung gegenüber dem Euro um 0,8 Prozent zu.

article.title: Opposition demands inquiry after Estrava's third rate hike
article.text: Estrava's main opposition party on Friday called for a parliamentary inquiry into the central bank's decision to raise its key rate to 4.5 percent. Party leader Dara Venn said homeowners with variable mortgages would pay hundreds of kessars more each month and accused the bank of reacting too late to inflation. The finance ministry said the central bank was independent and the government would not comment on its decisions.

article.title: Wildfire forces evacuation of 3,000 residents near Tarvos
article.text: A wildfire in the hills north of Tarvos forced authorities to evacuate around 3,000 residents on Saturday as strong winds pushed the flames towards three villages. More than 400 firefighters and six aircraft were deployed. The regional fire service said the blaze had burned 2,500 hectares since it started on Friday evening. No injuries were reported so far. The cause of the fire is unknown.

article.title: Tarvos wildfire contained after five days, police suspect arson
article.text: Firefighters have contained the wildfire north of Tarvos that forced 3,000 people from their homes last weekend, the regional fire service said on Wednesday. The fire burned around 4,100 hectares and destroyed 18 houses. Police said they had arrested a 34-year-old man suspected of starting the fire deliberately at two locations. Evacuated residents of the three villages were allowed to return home from Thursday.

article.text: Estrava's food safety agency on Tuesday ordered the recall of three batches of Velora infant formula after salmonella was found during routine testing at the company's plant in Harlund. assess.title: Estrava's parliament passes pension reform in 212-180 vote
assess.text: Estrava's parliament on Wednesday approved a pension reform that raises the statutory retirement age from 65 to 67 in steps between 2027 and 2035. The bill passed by 212 votes to 180, with 8 abstentions. Labour minister Teo Arval said the change would save about 3.2 billion kessars a year by 2035 according to the finance ministry's estimate, and that workers in physically demanding jobs could still retire at 63 with full benefits. The opposition announced a challenge before the constitutional court, arguing the transition was too short. Unions, which organised three national strike days against the plan, said they would support the legal challenge. The reform still needs the signature of the president, who has 15 days to sign or return it to parliament.

assess.title: Study of 48,000 adults links night-shift work to higher diabetes risk
assess.text: A study of 48,000 adults followed for twelve years found that people who regularly worked night shifts had a 19 percent higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes than day workers, after adjusting for age, body weight, smoking and income. The research, published on Monday in a peer-reviewed medical journal by a team at the University of Valmora, used national health records and employer data. The authors said the study showed an association, not proof of cause, and that self-reported diet data were a limitation. Lead author Dr. Ines Morrow said the results supported regular health checks for shift workers. Previous, smaller studies had found increases between 10 and 40 percent.
